What it says (English): What ANTIC and CIRT are and the laws behind them
Pidgin draft: ANTIC na di government office for Cameroon weh di look after ICT and cybersecurity. Dem get power from two laws weh dem sign on 21 December 2010: Law 2010/012 for cybersecurity and cybercrime, and Law 2010/013 for electronic communication. Dem head office dey for Bastos, Yaoundé. Inside ANTIC, di CIRT (CIRT-CM) na di team weh pipul talk to when dem get cyber problem. CIRT di send security warning, di teach pipul about cyber safety, di help pipul and business wen cyber wahala happen, and di help for investigation. Some ANTIC workers get special police power to write cybercrime and collect digital evidence.

What it says (English): How to contact CIRT-CM (8202, phone, email, form, link checker)
Pidgin draft: If yu wan contact CIRT-CM, use any of dese: call 8202, e free and e open day and night. Or call +237 222 207 909. Or send email to alerts@cirt.antic.cm. Or fill di report form for incident.cirt.cm. If yu wan check if one link or account safe, go check.cirt.cm. For serious case, yu fit go for ANTIC office. Wen yu no sure, na CIRT-CM be di correct place to ask for Cameroon.

What it says (English): What phishing is and how scammers create fear and hurry
Pidgin draft: Phishing na di scam weh pass for Cameroon. Di scammer di pretend say na MTN, Orange, yu bank, government or even yu friend, so dat dem go take yu money or yu secret information. Dem di send am by SMS, WhatsApp, email or phone call. Dem always want make yu fear or hurry: 'dem go block yu account', 'yu don win prize', 'package dey wait for yu'. If somebody di rush yu, be careful — real company no di force yu do something now-now.

What it says (English): Common local scams: fake lottery, free data, fake bank email, fake agent, fake scholarship, love scam
Pidgin draft: Scam weh pass for Cameroon: SMS weh say yu win lottery but yu must send 'processing fee' first. WhatsApp message wit free data weh carry yu go fake login page. Fake bank email weh say dem go close yu account if yu no 'verify' for di link. Person weh call say na Mobile Money agent and ask for yu PIN to 'fix problem'. Fake scholarship for social media weh ask 'processing fee'. And love scam, weh somebody make love wit yu for internet before e ask yu for money.

What it says (English): How to protect yourself from phishing and where to report
Pidgin draft: How yu go protect yusef: check di real number or address weh send di message, no only di name. No click link weh come by SMS or WhatsApp from number yu no know. Real company no di ask for yu password or PIN on phone. If yu no sure, call di company back wit di official number — no use di number weh dey for di strange message. If offer too sweet to be true, na scam. Report am to CIRT-CM (8202 free, or alerts@cirt.antic.cm) and keep screenshot as evidence.

What it says (English): Mobile Money scams: mistaken transfer, fake agent, prize SMS, fake link, fake seller
Pidgin draft: Mobile Money (MTN MoMo, Orange Money, Express Union Mobile) na di main way weh pipul di pay for Cameroon, so scammers like am well well. Scam weh pass: 'mistaken transfer' — stranger send yu money 'by mistake' and beg yu make yu send am back, but later dem reverse di first transfer so yu lose yu own money. Fake agent weh call say na MTN or Orange and tell yu make yu dial USSD code to 'update account' — but di code di send yu balance go dem. Fake prize SMS weh tell yu dial code to 'collect' di prize. Fake WhatsApp link wit Mobile Money bonus weh steal yu login. And fake seller weh ask yu 'confirm payment' wit code weh na transfer.

What it says (English): Golden rules for Mobile Money safety
Pidgin draft: Golden rules for Mobile Money: no ever give yu PIN to anybody, even person weh say na shop agent. Always check di name and number of di person before yu confirm transfer. No dial any USSD code weh stranger read for phone. Check yu transaction history often. If something look wrong, call yu operator official customer service now-now — no call number weh dem send yu by SMS. Change yu PIN from time to time. If somebody take yu money, call 8202 (CIRT-CM) or yu operator quick-quick.

What it says (English): Strong passwords, no reuse, weak examples, password manager
Pidgin draft: Password na di first door for yu account. Plenty pipul for Cameroon di use weak password — 1234, dem birth date or di name of dem quarter — and na dat one attacker di try first. Strong password must get at least 12 characters wit big letter, small letter, number and symbol (!@#$%&*). No use di same password for plenty accounts: if thief break one, e go try di same password for yu email and di rest. No use 'password', phone number, city plus birth year, football club plus year or 'iloveyou'. Better take one sentence weh yu know and change some letters to symbol. Use free password manager like Bitwarden or KeePass — den yu go remember only one master password.

What it says (English): What 2FA is and the WhatsApp / Mobile Money code traps
Pidgin draft: Two-factor authentication (2FA) na like second lock for door: even if thief know yu password, e still need one code to enter. CIRT-CM say na one of di best way to stop account hacking. For Cameroon, WhatsApp and Facebook account di hack plenty, and 2FA go stop most of dem. Trap weh pass: somebody message yu for WhatsApp say e send code to yu number 'by mistake' and beg yu make yu send am back. Dat code na yu own WhatsApp code — if yu give am, di person go take yu account and scam yu contacts. Same for SMS weh say yu Mobile Money don block and ask yu make yu send code. No answer am.

What it says (English): SIM-swap warning, how to switch on 2FA, never share an OTP
Pidgin draft: Fake telecom 'technician' fit call and ask yu make yu read SMS code 'to secure yu line' — dat one na SIM-swap. To put 2FA: for WhatsApp go Settings → Account → Two-step verification and put 6-digit PIN. For Facebook: Settings → Security and Login → Two-Factor Authentication. For Gmail: Google Account → Security → Two-Step Verification. For Instagram: Settings → Security → Two-Factor Authentication. No ever give OTP code weh come by SMS to anybody, even yu friend or 'agent'. If e possible, use authenticator app (Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator) — e strong pass SMS code and e work even without internet.

What it says (English): Risky things people post, privacy settings, Facebook View As
Pidgin draft: Cameroonians di use Facebook, WhatsApp, TikTok and Instagram plenty, and scammers di use wetin yu post to pretend say na yu or to trick yu: birth date, work place, school, quarter, family photo, travel plan. Things weh pipul di post without know: photo of ID card or passport, plane ticket wit name, 'I di travel for two weeks' (house empty!), photo of work screen, live location, and pikin wit school uniform and school name. Settings weh help: put 'Friends only' for Facebook, off location for photo, check who fit see yu number for WhatsApp (Settings → Privacy), no accept friend request from stranger, and delete old post weh get sensitive information. To see wetin stranger fit see for yu profile, use Facebook 'View As'.

What it says (English): How malware spreads and how to protect phone and computer
Pidgin draft: Virus (malware) di spread for Cameroon mostly through file weh pipul download from bad site, USB flash weh pipul share, APK weh dem install outside Play Store, and email attachment. Infected phone or computer fit spy on yu, steal yu login, and send fake SMS to yu contacts. USB flash na big problem for cybercafé, university and office. Bad sources: free movie or app from torrent site, 'free' APK weh dem share for Telegram or WhatsApp, USB weh yu no know, attachment from stranger, pop-up ad weh say e go make yu phone fast, and 'cracked' antivirus. How to protect yusef: install good antivirus (Avast free, Kaspersky, Bitdefender or ESET), download app only from Play Store or App Store, scan USB before yu open am, use Windows Defender, and for Android off 'Unknown sources' and on Google Play Protect.

What it says (English): What ransomware is and the 3-2-1 backup rule
Pidgin draft: Ransomware na virus weh lock all yu files and di attacker ask for money — usually Bitcoin — before e free dem. If yu no get backup, yu fit lose yu photo, document and work file forever. Business for Cameroon don lose millions of FCFA. Even person fit lose all family photo if phone spoil or dem steal am and no backup. Use di '3-2-1' rule: keep 3 copy of yu data (di original plus 2 backup), for 2 different kind of place (example external hard drive plus cloud), and 1 copy for different place (cloud). Free cloud: Google Drive (15 GB), OneDrive (5 GB), Mega (20 GB). Make backup every week for personal use; business must make am every day. Android: Settings → Google → Backup. WhatsApp: Settings → Chats → Chat backup → Back up to Google Drive.

What it says (English): What to report and what to do before reporting
Pidgin draft: If dem hack yu email or social media, steal yu identity, scam yu for Mobile Money or bank card, blackmail or harass yu online, or leak yu personal data — yu fit report to CIRT-CM. If e touch yu personal data, yu account or yu money, e good make yu report am. Before yu report, do dis quick: change password of di account weh dem touch, put 2FA if e no dey, tell yu bank or Mobile Money operator if money don go, and keep all evidence — screenshot, phone number, email, link and chat. No delete anything, even if e pain yu to look am.

What it says (English): How to submit the report and the contact channels
Pidgin draft: To report: send email to alerts@cirt.antic.cm, call 8202 (free, day and night) or +237 222 207 909, fill di form for incident.cirt.cm, or go for ANTIC office. To check if one link or account safe, use check.cirt.cm. If big money loss or serious identity theft, go for police too.
